fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to allow full-width vehicle passage.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or debris so emergency vehicles can reach the residence without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence to create a clear working space around the exterior walls.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to create a clear working space around its exterior walls.
• Mark any rear access points, gates, or pathways so responders can locate alternate routes to the back of the property without delay.
• Keep any gates or barriers along the rear access path unlocked or equipped with a standardized lock box so responders are not blocked from reaching the rear of the property.
• Trim vegetation along the walkway to keep it passable for responders moving between the front entry and other areas of the property.
• Identify a clear, level area near the access drive where emergency vehicles can stage without blocking the route to the residence.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees on all sides of the structure to create more open space between the canopy and the building.
• Remove woody debris piles visible near the structure, including downed branches and accumulated dead material.
• Trim branches from large trees that extend directly over or toward the roofline.
• Separate tree clusters near the structure by removing individual trees to break up the continuous canopy.
• Clear shrubs and low vegetation growing directly against the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin the understory beneath large trees near the structure to reduce the amount of burnable material at ground level.
• Remove dead branches from the lower portions of large trees closest to the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation on both sides.
• Maintain enough clearance along the driveway for emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the edges of the access route to keep the path visible and passable.
• Move any stored materials, firewood, or combustible items away from the base of the structure and outbuildings.
• Thin scattered trees in the open terrain nearest the structure to reduce the amount of continuous burnable material approaching the building.
